analysis:
Both supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (base lines 452-846). No patch hunks or head text were included, so the actual modification cannot be seen. I found nothing in the visible base text that is a security regression, new attack surface or invalidated assumption, and I cannot rule out one in the unseen diff. The file is documentation only, with no executable code or configuration.

The excerpt describes controls the integration pass should check against any code in this PR:
- SSD prefix-cache TTL raised from 15 to 30 minutes, recorded as the SEC-035 re-acceptance (T-041). The T-041 base definition already states 30 minutes.
- Default SSD write budget raised to 750 GB/day.
- App Attest protocol-3-only serving, build qualification, revocation fencing and key rotation (TB-011, T-052..T-058, A-015..A-017).
- Removal of the unauthenticated provider-earnings lookup (T-031).
- Attestation challenges now fail closed.
- Python-era wire fields removed.
- The minimum provider version floor now also excludes providers that report no version.
- Account-scoped first-content SLA.
- Advisory threat-model review workflow, which executes only the trusted base revision.

If other files in the PR change these behaviors, the integration pass should confirm that the threat-model entries (T-041, TB-011, T-053, T-054) remain accurate. I did not cross-check any changelog claim against source. Coverage limit: no diff content was supplied, so needs_deeper_review is true for the unseen modifications.
